tips.comment: Dannick is the most experienced in the field, having run six times and was placed in both starts on the all-weather this season. Last time, he was only beaten a neck when 2nd over 6f at Lingfield. He does his best work at the finish, and seven furlongs suit him better.

Call Me Betty was only 7th on debut at Redcar in May. That was over 6 furlongs, but she improved for the step up to 7 furlongs when 2nd at Thirsk earlier this month. That looks the best form on offer, and she looks the most likely winner here.

This horse won last time out when staying on strongly and getting up on the line. This horse gets just a 3lb rise for that win, and I fancy with a strong run race, this horse will get the pace to run at and can win again.

This is a weak affair so even though it was only a four runner race when SYDNEY WHISTLER was beaten by a length over this trip on handicap debut back in February, I still think he's worth a look off the back of that. Has had a flunk since then but at this price, a speculative each-way bet is in order.

Bold Suitor was gaining his 4th career win when winning over course and distance in March. He has been placed in 4 of his 5 starts since, including when second here earlier this month. Off the same mark, he must have a good chance of another win.
Done no favours by the draw last time out, but still ran well in the circumstances. Better drawn today and Doyle booked, can go close.
Back down to last winning mark, weighted to go well. I think this one is going to cause the upset in the race tomorrow.

Sent off favorite over course and distance in March 2025 and 2nd of 12 in a 3-year-old handicap. Disappointed at Lingfield next time out where the track may not have suited and weakened close to home over a mile at Windsor last time out. Given another chance, dropped in trip and back on the Wolverhampton Tapeta.

A hit-and-miss sort that I usually go for, CHEESE THE ONE is chanced from only a pound higher than the seasonal and stable debut when she was narrowly beaten over this trip. A total non-factor over the same trip next time out, but there is a previous course win here. So if we catch this unpredictable mare on a going day, we might get lucky.

23-May-25 h7 p1 p2 p9 h2 p2 Form Runs. MR 55 63 Adj MR. Recent race record 42%. Probability of winning is 33%. Running Style Prom at 67%. Actual win% 17%. Actual Place% is 50%. My win odds 5/1. My Place odds 7/1.
Failed to bring up a hat trick last time when on turf. He reverts back to AW here, where he seems to have the best form. Has a good each-way chance in this.

Dapper Gee Gee has only been with Tony Carroll since April. He is lightly raced, but Tony has found the key to him. The horse won at Chepstow in a 0-78 handicap over 7 furlongs and, on breeding, should stay this extra trip. He has a skillful jockey in Sara Bowen, and she will need to be very alert drawn 13. His getaway could be key to the whole result. Let's go NAP at 9/1 with four places each way.

Backing Northbound, the seasoned 7-year-old Fast Company gelding trained by Roger Fell and set to navigate a big field over 1 m 142 y in tomorrow’s Amateur Jockeys’ Handicap. He arrives off a solid winning return to action on the Wolverhampton Tapeta in April??'scoring comfortably in a 12-runner Class 6 contest off a mark in the mid-50s. That winter break seems to have freshened him up, and he’s since delivered consistent efforts with a sixth at Southwell and a fourth at Wolverhampton under a similar mark.
With an official rating around 63, he looks well treated given his resurgence this spring, and Roger Fell’s runners handle this Tapeta course well. Expect a patient ride from amateur jockey Miss Rosie Howarth, settling mid-pack before using his proven stamina to grind into contention late. Wolverhampton’s flat, even surface should play to his strengths, and at around 20/1, he offers appealing each-way value in a deep field.

This 5-year-old has had a few ups and downs. He was a C&D winner in April but finished last in a handicap here 20 days ago. He has potential if he shows up on a good day, but it's tough to say if he will perform at his best. My assessment will be based on jockey Lauren Frost, who has competed at Wolverhampton 4 times, achieving 1 victory and 2 places. Her 5lb claim is beneficial, making an each-way bet at 20/1 look quite promising.

Trainer Andrew Balding, currently performing well, showcases this 2-year-old closely linked to the 1 mile winner September Leaves, and a half-brother to winners Cosa Sara and Grappa Nonino. There's much to admire on paper, and significant confidence in the betting would be telling. He sports cheekpieces and will be ridden by Probert.
Alfa Duplicate did well when second up in a big money C2 when seventh. It could be worth another shot now in a C4 with the top draw.
Her only win came over this course and distance last September, and she should be able to win from this mark. The one to beat in this race.

Shiplake represents powerful connections in Amo Racing. This colt left his debut form behind when landing a Newcastle novice event in November, keeping on well. That run came when dropping in trip to today's distance and was also his first outing on today's surface, Tapeta. Kept in the same class today. more will be expected of this colt who may turn out to be better than a Class 5 horse. His stable has saddled two winners in the last three days.

HAVE I TOLD YOU is drawn widest which may force her hand. She is an Irish trained filly who represents a yard who tried landing some bets with a flat handicapper on Sunday. Some from this yard have shown up well recently including at the recent Ascot meeting , so the market can tell us more.

Turf runs have not gone to plan, so should welcome a return back to AW, which is helped by gaining valuable experience over C&D when a useful 2 of 8 back in April of this year, which was off a higher mark.

There are plenty of unknowns in this one: seasonal returners, debutants on the AW, and so on. But the selection is a course winner and impressed in that race and also over this trip at Kempton when staying on despite having no luck in running. I would be happier if Kingscote was available in the saddle, but Costello's record here is better than some. I would be shocked if outside the first 4.

Daughter of Mohaather & Kerry's Dream ( Dam's sire Tobougg ) who was last seen at Lingfield 20 days ago where finishing 6th/8 however that was her second outing after a 194 day break and she now arrives here in top fitness and ready to get competitive especially having found a suitable assignment here steps back up in trip going over the 6 furlong trip that being a positive move by her connections as she can be seen to best effect over this trip in a race that should be run to suit Skellig Isle's nature of going very well given the horses enrolled to run here currently operating on an easing mark of 70 T Ward's inmate can bounce back and make her presence strongly felt in this class 5 handicap jockey Alec Voikhansky takes off a handy 3lb which can only help her cause here must be taken seriously and accordingly and by no means underestimated here . Respected .

This lad is still seeking his first win but has run with credit in both his AW handicaps. On handicap debut over C&D, he shaped well before having to give the winner first run in the straight in order to get off the rail and attack, and was beaten half a length and clear of the field. At Newcastle this year, he was ridden too far back and faded over the last furlong, having done too much to get there, and will probably prefer the tighter track here anyway. Now 4 lbs lower than in that debut here in September, he has a better jockey than for either of those rides, a good draw, and every chance.

Saturn Five's last run was too bad to be true. Was up with the pace but never got going and was eased from over 2f out. The lightly-raced 6-y-o showed encouraging form in his three previous races off marks of 74, 76, and 77. Races off a career-low of 71 today with Callum Shepherd aboard for the first time.

Beaten a length when 3rd of 7 over course and distance under today's jockey off a 4-pound higher mark in March 2025. Went third close to home over a mile and a quarter at Yarmouth last time out too and should go well back at this trip and distance off this lower mark.

Course and distance winner who was last seen at Yarmouth 32 days ago where finishing a creditable 3rd/8 now returning to the all weather track here at Wolverhampton R Spencer's inmate will really appreciate this return to an all weather surface as he is most certainly a better performer on the all weather rather than the turf currently operating on a very handy mark of 67 Con Te Partiro looks poised to strike here and worth noting he is now operating 2lb below his last winning mark this is a straightforward assignment for this gelded son of Time Test & Groovejet ( Dam's sire Cockney Rebel ) that shouldn't take much winning as it is a pretty thin class 5 handicap and Con Te Partiro who possesses all the necessary credentials in the field can take an assignment of this nature and get back on the score boards jockey Hollie Doyle takes the ride and will give this a good shot merits serious consideration here

Wadacre Grace tends to do most of her winning on Poly but is now back on her last winning mark and was a decent second here last December when running against the boys off a 68. She could be worth an EW 4P off today's 67.
Tongue strap on LTO did not have the desired effect when only 9 of 13 at Southwell last August. But now with a new yard and been off for 10 months, so expecting good things from this horse.

Just five career runs for the 3yo filly. She was 2nd and 4th in her last two races, only outpaced late on last time out and this shorter trip should suit her. The winners from those last two races have both given the form a nice boost since. Room for improvement and this low grade 0-50 handicap is very winnable.

Won over course and distance under today's jockey off this mark of 50 back in July 2024. Went up 7 pounds as a consequence of that success and struggled as a result. 2 runs in the last 6 weeks following a 204 day break will see her much fitter today and she could go well dropping in trip off this winning mark.

Veteran sprinter Endowed comes here after winning over course and distance 7 days ago. The John Flint gelding showed a likeable attitude to get his grey head back into the winner's enclosure after 3 years in the doldrums. That performance showed the one-time 90-rated sprinter still retains plenty of zest for the game. Callum Hutchinson retains the partnership, taking over from the jockey/owner I Mathias (5lb). Hutchinson's only mount of the day looks to have an excellent opportunity to follow up last week's victory.
I thought Oldbury Lad was desperately unlucky when hampered by the eventual winner last time out at Salisbury. He showed guts by digging in and passing three or four to claim second.

The 3yo filly was 2nd of 12 four weeks ago, no chance behind a smart winner but she had the measure of the rest. It was her handicap debut, just a second run this year and just a fourth career run. More to come from this one in this low grade contest.

Diamond Cottage did well here under Gina when winning last month on good off a 47 but could not follow up last time out off a 50 on soft. But I think the firmer ground today could see her bounce back each way.

Coming here in dodgy form but is a 2 time C&D winner and 4lbs lighter than last winning mark but has a 5lb claimer so in truth net difference is -9lbs. Despite form; I do think she can win tomorrow off current mark.

Since being gelded, the 3-year-old has demonstrated a new level of performance, achieving 2 respectable placements before finally securing a victory in a 6f Haydock handicap 32 days ago. He travelled smoothly and finished strong defeating a horse that won its next outing. He is expected to deliver another impressive run.

Just 6 career starts for the 3yo. His AW form reads 0231. He was only beaten 1/2L on turf five weeks ago in a decent 12 runner handicap, losing out in the last strides. Same mark for this race, this handicap is not as strong, room for improvement and the drop in trip should suit him.

First time running over 6f. Has been in good form for new trainer as of late, so I'm assuming they must feel this step up in trip is something hard to look past. In my opinion, I have a very good eye for noticing things like this. I could be wrong, but I'm going with my gut for this one to outrun its odds and run a blinder.

Ten Club is another that won here in May in a C5 on good but could not follow up last time in a C4 on soft. The return to C5 today on GF could see him bounce back, and he has won off this mark on the AW. EW

Four runs this year for the 4-year-old filly, only beaten 2L in her last two races and seems in good shape. Good/soft ground last time out. Down to a handy mark now, strong jockey booking. Her three highest RPR ratings last year came on this quick ground.

Temperamental type who refused to run back in March of this year. But no doubt he has some ability. However, starting to get well handicapped, which is making life hard and reflects stats of just 3 wins from 27 runs. Also going through a barren run, but dropped mark presents an opening.

All Ways Glamorous has done well in the last four runs, reading 1218, with the latest being pants after a duff start while stepping up to C4. I think the return here, where he won in May while back in a C5 today, could see him bounce back.
Close to a bet to nothing, So Smart looks a bet with Eddie Greaterex riding for Grace Harris. This CD winner ran a cracker last time, and this is a drop in class.

5-time course winner (3 CD) who is yet to strike this season but was beaten less than a length on each of her 3 visits here. Dropped a lb for a really solid 2nd last time and so will surely take all the beating this afternoon.
Honour Your Dreams for me is the one to beat. Form has been franked, dropping back down to 5f with ideal ground conditions. Nice price on offer as well here.

Goes well over course and distance, including when winning here two starts ago. Just 1 lb higher today and not disgraced last time out on going that was likely much softer than the reported good to soft. Conditions here are more suitable and could have plenty of pace to aim at as well.

A decent debut at the start of the month from the 2yo filly. She was 5th of 12, very green early on but stayed on nicely from the rear, not far from being placed, the race won by a smart looking type. She should be better for the run. That race was a £16K maiden race and this novice stakes looks very weak. Good jockey change, strong stable.

Zoulu Chief has not won since winning three times as a two-year-old, but he has been running at a high level. He has finally dropped below his last winning mark and has had wind surgery since his last run at York in May. He should go close.

This R Hughes-trained 5-year-old gelding is the winner of three races over five furlongs on good to firm ground and on the all-weather. After finding trouble in running when beaten six lengths behind the J & S Quinn-trained J M Jungle in his latest race over five furlongs on good ground at Epsom, down in class with Oisin Murphy booked, a win looks more than likely.
CD winner now running at its favorite mark. From 3 runs at this mark, has won twice on today's conditions. Jockey rode 4 times, is yet to win on this horse. Each way play.

Outsider of the party here, but back to last winning mark. Recent efforts are not as bad as they seem in the context of today's conditions. Was going well in better sprints than this last year off higher. Interesting in new headgear. Marquand back in the saddle for the first time since the last win.
Orionis runs in her first handicap after hacking up at Ripon at 1-14 in a weak maiden. Her mark of 77 looks fair and she should follow up against three older opponents.

This A M Balding-trained 3-year-old filly won her first race in her latest start over one mile two furlongs on good to firm ground at Redcar 27 days ago. She stayed on well in the closing stages to beat the J L Flint-trained Spirit Of The Bay by 1 1/4 lengths. With Oisin Murphy onboard for the first time, she looks hard to oppose.

Roger Varian is currently enjoying his best period of the season, and he has a good chance of maintaining that run with Silent City in this maiden. Silent City didn't make it to the track as a two year old, only making her racecourse debut at Goodwood just over a fortnight ago. She was understandably green that day, but will have learned plenty. Interestingly she was ridden by a very inexperienced jockey that day, whereas she has the benefit of former champion Silvestre De Sousa aboard this time. The price looks short enough, but I'll be happy to collect.

Read All About It has placed once in two starts and stands a very good chance again today. Ran a decent race when 2nd last time out. Tom Marquand is booked, which is encouraging. Distance and ground suit also. E/W prospect.
Southbank looks a solid pick from what looks on paper a weak enough race. No one is standing out to be a serious contender for me.

Three-time C&D winner Lequinto races off a career-low of 58 today, and with a further 7lb claim deducted, could be ready to open apprentice jockey Mathew Lloyd Slater's account. Underwent wind surgery before last outing too. In to 9's from 12/1 overnight.

Vape should have won under Oisin Murphy the time before, and it was odd that a young lad on his first ride was put up next time. A bit of cash came for it, but the ground had deteriorated by then. Below its winning mark, that young lad is up again? Not going heavy, but the ground is better here. Small each way.

At the top third of the handicap mark with a 3lb claimer and dropping down in class tomorrow. In truth, he will need everything in his favor considering the barren run, which now stretches to 21 runs since his last win back in 2023. The current mark gives a lot of encouragement that he can finally break that barren run.

LITTLE MISS MAGIC is considered down in grade from a mark below last season's peak, which included a narrow defeat on her last run over this trip last September. Could be considered on return here for a stable that usually do well with their sprinters. Looks to be handily drawn from a high stall also and there's extra places to seek out too.

Libra Tiger has only had a couple of runs this year at Lingfield on the all-weather since last September. His latest run in April was poor; he faded to a distant last of five. He is better than that, and the handicapper reacted by dropping him a further three pounds to a new low mark of 57. His last win was off 65 over 6f at Kempton in March 2024, but his only win on turf came over 5f at Sandown off 68 when with Ed Walker in July 2023. Laura Mangan utilizes Alfie Redman to take off five pounds, and he has had 4 wins from 44 rides.

Although she remains a maiden after 8 tries, recent performances suggest her breakthrough could be imminent. She secured a commendable 2nd place in a handicap at Bath just 9 days ago, finishing clear of the rest. Following that effort, she has been increased by 3lb, yet she still holds considerable appeal, particularly with Shoemark riding.

Bondi comes here on handicap debut, being stepped up in trip 3f. The trainer often suggests stepping his horses up in trip is a positive. Dam's stamina suggests this trip should be ideal. Has shaped with promise in maiden company. I think if the market speaks positively as well, this should be the one to beat.

Hes the most exposed in the field being placed in 5 of his 6 career runs so far between 7-10f only run didn't place was 22 days ago finishing 2nd of 4 & beaten 3.5L over 8f . J.O'Brien reaches for the blinkers today for 1st time & horses main opposition will most probably come from his stable mate .
Made U Blush has shown promise in her first three outings when today's jockey was aboard. Although a ten-length fifth of sixteen at Cork seven weeks ago, she plugged on well.

Lady Plimsoll looks interesting in this, arrives with the best recent form after finishing 4th over this distance last time out. Still unexposed on turf, probably has more to offer. Just a little improvement and she'll be running well.

Sugar Club had a fair season last year winning a ten runner maiden at Bellewstown following a third of ten on debut. Has hit the rails a bit since, especially this year but I'm hoping that today's first-time cheekpieces have the desired effect.

This is a race for Apprentice jockeys, this horse has one of the better Apprentice jockeys in the saddle. The horse isn't fully proven at this distance but he had no problems getting this distance on his 1 previous attempt at this distance, should have more to offer at this distance. This race looks easier than his last.

Ina Mina is a 4-year-old filly who is 0-15 wins but has placed twice over today's trip and good ground. She makes her second start for Michael Mulvany, who makes hay at Ballinrobe with 5/15 wins in 8f+ handicaps. Her best over today's trip came when finishing 2/10 at Clonmel in a maiden, posting an RPR of 75. So today's 62 with Wesley Joyce shouldn't hold any fears. With the trip and going proving suitable, this filly could be chucked in at the weights for just her second start for the yard, who do well at Ballinrobe.

The only CD winner in the field is Brewel Hill, which is reunited with that day's winner, S Foley. Ridden by an apprentice on season debut, it was smart away, fading late on. So it will be much fitter today and looks overpriced in context, back on that winning mark.

I’m not saying CASANOVA can win, but I do think he can leave some of that old form behind. He’s been racing on soft ground of late (last 3 runs) and his best form, and indeed winning form, is on a sounder surface. The forecast is ‘good’ with light or little overnight rain, so there are risks involved. This is his trip. He’s a 3-time winner, he’s 6 lbs below his last winning mark. One more positive is Adam Caffrey is back on board. He rides most winners for Ado. Lots of risks, but 25/1 is juicy.

Ozark Daze put in a solid effort last time out at Ballinrobe, finishing third in a competitive 11-runner field. Having been tested over extended trips in recent outings, he now drops back to a more manageable 1m 1f ??' a move that could play to his strengths, especially given his proven stamina.
In his most recent start at Roscommon, Ozark Daze finished just a length behind Ragmans Corner ??' a notable performance considering that rival, ridden by Colin Keane, has since gone on to win a large-field handicap (21 runners) at Navan. That form gives the run some solid substance.
James Ryan retains the ride, and while he’s still seeking his first win aboard Ozark Daze, his valuable 3lb claim and growing experience could prove a significant asset. With conditions likely to suit and the drop back in trip looking a smart move, Ozark Daze could well be in the mix at an attractive price.

He placed 15th in a handicap at Limerick 59 days ago, beginning slowly. Now wearing cheekpieces for the first time, he stands a good chance of this mark if he can recover. Nonetheless, he has a fair amount to demonstrate at this time, but Ciaran Murphy tends to do well when he enters just one runner in a flat meeting. Therefore, I will support Murphy with a modest each-way bet at 40/1.
Dual-purpose horse who won on the flat off 64, 3 runs back. Followed that up with a win over hurdles before being outclassed in a decent novice LTO. Chance off 69 with Keane booked.
Preparations from the Slattery yard looked like a stayer when plugging on throughout last time and goes a further furlong here. EW

The Mediator is an 8-year-old gelding trained by Gordon Elliott. He is a useful dual-purpose horse, a bumper winner, and a comfortable winner of a maiden hurdle just three starts back. Yet to win on the flat in seven attempts, he has placed four times in the top four over further than today's 13f, posting a career-high RPR of 79. So there will be no doubt about today's trip or handicap mark of 69, and he clearly handles today's good ground.

POWERFUL HOOK HEAD has been gelded and takes his chance with the yard in fine form and a jockey in DBM who rides Ballinrobe at least as well as any other pilot. This racer is only a lightly-raced maiden , but has a workable mark as a result and the post-time market should tell us more.

KHORMOR SYD raced last time out as if a longer trip would suit. He was in Claiming company that day and now handicapping from his current mark seems within his reach. Experienced pilot Billy Lee rode him last time presumably providing feedback , so the market could reveal more.

This is the first run since departing from the Harty stable, where the 5-year-old finished last in a handicap at Limerick just 12 days ago. Now returning to a shorter distance, if James Barcoe can revive this distance winner's form from 2024, these enticing odds of 50/1 could yield a profit from an each-way bet.

Beaten only by one who is bordering on Pattern class the last time she tackled 12f, back in October and wasn't stopping. So this extra furlong should not be an issue. Makes handicap debut off 83, which she would need to improve to land this, but she won her maiden easily last time with the runner-up winning next time.

Last year's winner, Royal Eagle, looks to have a good chance of a repeat success. She won off a mark of 77 last year and also won at Bellewstown in August off 81. Campaigned over hurdles since, she had been placed 3 times before winning last month at Listowel. Returned to the flat off 83, she looks a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

Fratas is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Michael Mulvany and knows how to get the job done, winning 5 out of 18 on turf. He will definitely stay this 13f, having picked up a maiden hurdle on debut. He sits 2lb below his last winning mark of 83 on 81 and comes here in good heart, having finished 2-2-2 in his last three starts. This useful dual-purpose horse could well play a big part in proceedings under Wesley Joyce and his yard.

Last Chance Saloon for this one to recapture his form from last year, in the hope that she has needed her 2 runs this year. Drops another pound here and now just than when winning on her last run of last season.

This 4 year old shows considerable promise. Although he remains a maiden after 7 flat races, he achieved a respectable 4th place in a handicap at Leopardstown 18 days ago, where he was left with much to do. He sets a strong standard and is a prime candidate with Keane on board.

Bottom weight Ainm Bentley is a wild swing here. Missed the break LTO in Gowran but responded well to pressure after being last into the straight, staying on up the hill to finish 7th of 15, beaten by 9 lengths. The extra furlong and the first-time blinkers might bring about a bit of improvement. Kieran Purcell has retained Martin Hassett, and that 5lb claim ensures this bottom-rated gets a nice pull off these. All the risks, but at 50/1, all the rewards.
